subject: Copywriting
title: Rolls-Royce: The Ogilvy Standard
description: Learn Rolls-Royce: The Ogilvy Standard in one minute.

hook.text: 'At 60 mph, the loudest noise comes from the electric clock.' Ogilvy's Rolls-Royce headline set the gold standard.

buildup.text: David Ogilvy spent three weeks researching the car before writing.

discovery.text: The ad was 607 words of pure fact. Every sentence was a proof point. Ogilvy sold luxury through engineering specificity.

twist.text: A Rolls-Royce engineer reportedly said: 'We really must do something about that clock.' They missed the point—the ad.

climax.text: Ogilvy proved that luxury copy doesn't need poetry.

punchline.text: 607 factual words. 104 headlines tested. One clock made it legendary.

quiz.question: How many headlines did Ogilvy test for the Rolls-Royce ad?

details.summary: David Ogilvy's Rolls-Royce headline — 'At 60 miles an hour the loudest noise in this new Rolls-Royce comes from the electric clock' — is the most famous luxury car ad ever written. The line works by proving quality through a single hyper-specific detail. Ogilvy spent three weeks researching the...
details.whyItMatters: The Rolls-Royce ad proves that specificity is the soul of luxury copy. One researched, concrete detail persuades more than a thousand superlatives.
takeaways: Ogilvy's Rolls-Royce headline is considered the finest car ad ever written
The power comes from one hyper-specific, researched detail
Three weeks of research produced a single line that sold thousands of cars

faq.question: Why is the Rolls-Royce headline considered the best ever?
faq.answer: It communicates supreme quality through a single, verifiable detail rather than vague superlatives. 'The loudest noise comes from the electric clock' makes readers imagine the silence — and therefore the engineering perfection — for themselves. It shows rather than tells.

faq.question: What does the ad teach about luxury copywriting?
faq.answer: Research creates great copy. Ogilvy read everything about the car until he found the one detail that communicated the brand's essence. Luxury copywriters must understand the product deeply enough to find the single detail that says everything.
